front_blocks.md: Define **development**.

back_blocks.md: The **progress or improvements** a country makes that improve people's lives and make the country more independent.

cards.front_md: Define **development**.
cards.back_md: The **progress or improvements** a country makes that improve people's lives and make the country more independent.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Development is a smooth, continuous process.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Development can be slowed, halted or even reversed by factors such as war, disease, disasters and economic recession.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Development is a smooth, continuous process.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Development can be slowed, halted or even reversed by factors such as war, disease, disasters and economic recession.

front_blocks.md: Name three factors that can slow, halt or reverse development.

back_blocks.md: **War/conflict**, **disease**, **disasters** and **economic recession**.

cards.front_md: Name three factors that can slow, halt or reverse development.
cards.back_md: **War/conflict**, **disease**, **disasters** and **economic recession**.

front_blocks.md: Define the **strands of development**.

back_blocks.md: The different areas in which a country progresses, not just wealth — **economic, demographic, social, cultural, political and environmental**.

cards.front_md: Define the **strands of development**.
cards.back_md: The different areas in which a country progresses, not just wealth — **economic, demographic, social, cultural, political and environmental**.

front_blocks.md: Economic development depends on resources, internal boosters and **______**.

back_blocks.md: Economic development depends on resources, internal boosters and **external boosters**.

cards.front_md: Economic development depends on resources, internal boosters and **______**.
cards.back_md: Economic development depends on resources, internal boosters and **external boosters**.

front_blocks.md: Define **external boosters**.

back_blocks.md: Influences from **outside a country** that boost economic development, such as **TNCs, globalisation and international agencies**.

cards.front_md: Define **external boosters**.
cards.back_md: Influences from **outside a country** that boost economic development, such as **TNCs, globalisation and international agencies**.

front_blocks.md: What three groups are countries placed in by level of development?

back_blocks.md: **Developed** (very high human development), **Emerging** (high or medium), and **Developing** (low human development).

cards.front_md: What three groups are countries placed in by level of development?
cards.back_md: **Developed** (very high human development), **Emerging** (high or medium), and **Developing** (low human development).

front_blocks.md: How does the cycle of wealth support development?

back_blocks.md: As the economy grows, people earn more, so the government collects more **taxes** and people have more **disposable income**; these taxes and business profits are **reinvested** in growth, infrastructure, education and healthcare.

cards.front_md: How does the cycle of wealth support development?
cards.back_md: As the economy grows, people earn more, so the government collects more **taxes** and people have more **disposable income**; these taxes and business profits are **reinvested** in growth, infrastructure, education and healthcare.

front_blocks.md: A stable and effective **______** also helps to lead to development.

back_blocks.md: A stable and effective **government** also helps to lead to development.

cards.front_md: A stable and effective **______** also helps to lead to development.
cards.back_md: A stable and effective **government** also helps to lead to development.

front_blocks.md: Define **human welfare**.

back_blocks.md: A person's **quality of life** — their overall well-being, including physical, social, economic and psychological components.

cards.front_md: Define **human welfare**.
cards.back_md: A person's **quality of life** — their overall well-being, including physical, social, economic and psychological components.

front_blocks.md: What four types of component make up quality of life?

back_blocks.md: **Physical**, **social**, **economic** and **psychological** components.

cards.front_md: What four types of component make up quality of life?
cards.back_md: **Physical**, **social**, **economic** and **psychological** components.

front_blocks.md: Define the **development gap**.

back_blocks.md: The **difference in levels of development** between the least developed and most developed countries in the world.

cards.front_md: Define the **development gap**.
cards.back_md: The **difference in levels of development** between the least developed and most developed countries in the world.

front_blocks.md: How many main stages of development does the UN identify?

back_blocks.md: **Four** main stages of development.

cards.front_md: How many main stages of development does the UN identify?
cards.back_md: **Four** main stages of development.

front_blocks.md: What is another name for emerging economies?

back_blocks.md: **Newly industrialised countries (NICs)**.

cards.front_md: What is another name for emerging economies?
cards.back_md: **Newly industrialised countries (NICs)**.

front_blocks.md: To be classed as a least developed country, a nation must have a Gross National Income below **______**.

back_blocks.md: To be classed as a least developed country, a nation must have a Gross National Income below **US\$1,018**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Landlocked countries generally develop faster than coastal countries.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Landlocked countries find **trade more difficult** and so often develop more slowly.

front_blocks.md: Define **natural resources**.

back_blocks.md: The things **provided by the physical environment**, such as water, forests, fossil fuels, soil, rocks, minerals and animals.

front_blocks.md: How does mechanisation of farming affect development?

front_blocks.md: Define **GDP per capita**.

back_blocks.md: The **total value of goods and services produced within a country in a year, divided by its population**.

cards.front_md: Define **GDP per capita**.

back_blocks.md: The **number of children per 1,000 who die below the age of 1**.

front_blocks.md: Why can GDP per capita hide inequality within a country?

back_blocks.md: It is an **average**, so the variation in wealth is hidden — two countries with the same GDP per capita can have very different distributions of wealth.

cards.front_md: Why can GDP per capita hide inequality within a country?

front_blocks.md: Define the **Human Development Index (HDI)**.

back_blocks.md: A **combined measure** of average achievement in health, education and standard of living.

cards.front_md: Define the **Human Development Index (HDI)**.
cards.back_md: A **combined measure** of average achievement in health, education and standard of living.

front_blocks.md: Between which two values is HDI scored?

back_blocks.md: **0 to 1** — the higher the HDI, the higher the level of development and quality of life.

cards.front_md: Between which two values is HDI scored?

front_blocks.md: What does the Gini coefficient index measure?

back_blocks.md: The **distribution of wealth** within a country, identifying where wealth distribution is most unequal.

A high Gini coefficient value means wealth is distributed more equally.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A **high value means the distribution of wealth is unequal**; a low value means it is more equal.
